findings: The exact two-component Hamiltonian, periodic laboratory-basis wavefunction, unrestricted global Gibbs state and equilibrium-before-infinite-gap limit define the physical kinetic-energy observable uniquely. No projection method or numerical representation is mandated.

In each exact laboratory Fourier block, up carries integer angular momentum n-q and down carries n. The lower local internal state has up population p=(1-cos(theta))/2. Its kinetic expectation is [(n-q*p)^2+q^2*p*(1-p)]/(2I). This independently gives both the shifted angular sectors and the diagonal scalar cost used by the oracle.

The source retains the complete local scalar kinetic cost but uses ordinary periodic scalar rotor sectors. It is a valid positive scalar Hamiltonian approximation that discards global internal-state holonomy. Even winding at pi/2 makes the connection integer, giving exact calibration equivalence; odd and tilted cases distinguish the models.

The independent verifier diagonalizes finite-gap laboratory-spin Fourier blocks and measures the original kinetic operator before inverse-gap extrapolation. It does not substitute total energy plus the gap at finite gap. An unsplit Fourier-matrix check confirms the block construction.

Public-domain boundary and interior checks bound inverse-gap reference error below 1.04e-8 and angular cutoff error below 4.5e-16. All 256 noisy fits pass correct predictions and reject the scalar-only closure; hidden gaps exceed 21 percent against 4 percent tolerance.

Local controls pass 8/8 for oracle and pass calibration/parameter/anchor checks while failing the three discriminating groups for the completed shortcut. Calibration objective is identified throughout the allowed inertia range; uncertainties are fixed instrument noise.

Removed the redundant public sentence highlighting calibration windings before source freezing; the public data still includes all measured control values. Hidden cases, true inertia, correction, private hint and author derivation remain outside the image.
